stories.headline: Cloudburst triggers flash flood in Kargil; mud and boulders sweep through stream
stories.title: Cloudburst triggers flash flood in Kargil; mud and boulders sweep through stream
stories.summary: Cloudburst triggers flash flood in Kargil; mud and boulders sweep through stream
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A cloudburst in Kargil's Stakpa Sankoo area sent a surge of water, mud and boulders through the local nallah.
The incident has renewed focus on the Himalayan region's exposure to sudden extreme weather events.
A cloudburst over Kargil's Stakpa Sankoo area has triggered a sudden surge of water in the stream passing through the region, sending a torrent of mud, boulders and other debris downstream.

The debris-laden floodwaters swept through the area as the sudden rise in water levels turned the nallah into a fast-moving channel, with the extent of damage and any casualties yet to be ascertained.

The incident comes as the Himalayan region remains under heightened scrutiny for extreme weather events, particularly flash floods and cloudbursts that can cause sudden and destructive surges in mountainous areas.

The Kargil incident also comes against the backdrop of the devastating flash floods in Nepal, where intense rainfall triggered floods and landslides across several areas, causing widespread destruction and a high number of casualties.
The Nepal disaster has also highlighted the vulnerability of Himalayan communities to sudden weather events, with rescue and relief operations continuing in several affected areas.
Further details on the situation in Stakpa Sankoo, including possible damage to roads, homes or infrastructure, are awaited.

stories.headline: Assam: Bal Raksha Bharat reaches 230 flood-affected families in Nazira
stories.title: Assam: Bal Raksha Bharat reaches 230 flood-affected families in Nazira
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: JORHAT: Bal Raksha Bharat has intensified its humanitarian response to the devastating Assam floods by reaching out to 230 of the most severely affected families in Gohai Bari and Komal Chapori village under Nazira sub-division of Sivasagar district, one of the worst-impacted localities in the district.

As part of its humanitarian response, Bal Raksha Bharat distributed food kits, shelter kits, and dignity and hygiene kits to flood-affected families who have been left struggling to recover from extensive damage to their homes, belongings, and livelihoods.
The humanitarian response also recognises that children require dedicated support in the aftermath of a disaster.
Bal Raksha Bharat is running a Child Friendly Space (CFS) in Komal Chapori, providing immediate, safe, and supportive activities for children aged 3–18 years.

The space enables children to remain active and engaged through play, recreational activities, and basic learning opportunities while their families focus on cleaning homes, replacing lost belongings, and rebuilding their lives.
Avinash Singh, Director of Programmes, Bal Raksha Bharat, said, “For families in Komal Chapori, the flood has not ended with the receding waters.
Many are returning to damaged homes, lost belongings, and an uncertain recovery.

Our response is therefore designed to go beyond immediate relief—providing food security, shelter support, and dignity while ensuring that children have a safe space to play, learn, and cope with the disruption around them.”

stories.headline: Rebuilt with India aid, flood-erased Nepal school seeks help to rebuild on higher ground
stories.title: Rebuilt with India aid, flood-erased Nepal school seeks help to rebuild on higher ground
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: TRISHULI BAZAAR (NUWAKOT, NEPAL): Three warnings came within minutes the day it flooded, an accountant rushed in saying water was gushing in, a teacher relayed a phone call from upstream saying the area had been “swallowed”, and a parent arrived on a scooter to take his daughter away.
Principal Rajendra Dawadi immediately ordered around 900 students at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School out.
They escaped before the river wiped out the 76-year-old campus.
Now, Dawadi, teachers and students agree on one thing: classes must restart at the earliest, but the school must never be rebuilt beside the river.
It has to rise on higher ground.
TOI on Sunday.
“When they look at it, they feel afraid.”
Close to a thousand people, including the children, had been inside the school when the warnings arrived.
Thirty girls were in the residential hostel.
When they asked Dawadi where they could go because their homes were far away, he told them to follow him uphill.
Dawadi ordered a non-teaching employee to ring the bell and teachers began clearing classrooms.
Staff helped students suffering panic attacks.

stories.title: China deleting Tibet flood videos amid questions over disaster, report claims

stories.headline: Rescued Indians recount near‑death escape as they return home after Nepal disaster
stories.title: Rescued Indians recount near‑death escape as they return home after Nepal disaster
stories.summary: Rescued tourists from West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Kerala recounted harrowing near-death experiences after being stranded during flash floods in Nepal. Many described landslides, buses swept away, and buildings collapsing before state governments facilitated their safe return home.
